title: Solar-memory models trained on Cycles 21–23 still underpredict F10.7 and Mg II in Cycle 25
abstract: We test whether solar memory explains the reported fall of sunspot number relative to emission indices. We fit nonlinear prompt-plus-decay models to daily SILSO V2 sunspot number, adjusted F10.7 and measured Bremen Mg II in Cycles 21–23. We then test later cycles without refitting. In common observation days of cycle months 36–82, the causal model underpredicts Cycle 25 F10.7 by 15.27 sfu (95 percent refitted block interval 11.36–19.89) and Mg II by 0.003285 (0.002665–0.003908). Monthly fits and a symmetric solar-rotation kernel retain the error. Memory improves the daily fit but does not remove the mean change. The model-implied sunspot factors needed to match the Cycle 25 means are 1.177 for F10.7 and 1.321 for Mg II. These are not recommended corrections. The tested fixed memory responses do not explain the full change. The cause remains open because solar structure, index calibration and model error can each contribute. The package includes code, source hashes, model results and a retrieval recipe. External observations remain outside the baseline publication.

display.caption: Model-implied sunspot multipliers in cycle months 36–82. Models are trained on Cycles 21–23. Bars for Cycles 24 and 25 show refitted 81-day block intervals. The factors are diagnostics, not corrections.
